title: Concurrent Bank Simulator
hints: `std::scoped_lock lock{ from.mutex, to.mutex };` locks both without the deadlock you get when one thread locks A then B and another locks B then A (lesson 12.02).
A transfer from an account to itself would lock the same mutex twice. Pick a different account when the two random numbers are equal.
requirements: 10 accounts with 1,000 each and 4 threads making 10,000 random transfers each
Version A: one mutex for the whole bank
Version B: one mutex per account, locked with `std::scoped_lock` so two accounts are always locked safely
After the threads finish, check that the total is still 10,000
Compare how long the two versions take
stretch: Remove the locking once and show the total going wrong; then a deliberately deadlocking lock order, and the fix.
